en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having one of the most perfectly symmetrical cone shapes in the world.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and one of the largest eagles in the world.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippines, containing the capital city of Manila and the Cordillera mountains.
Taal Lake in Batangas is a freshwater lake inside a large volcanic caldera that contains Volcano Island, which has its own crater lake.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley in northeastern Luzon.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the South China Sea.
The tamaraw, a small, V-horned buffalo endemic to the island of Mindoro, is critically endangered and strictly protected under Philippine wildlife laws.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season, resembling giant chocolate kisses.
The Philippines is a top global producer of nickel, with large open-pit nickel mines operating primarily in the provinces of Surigao and Palawan.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol and other Visayan islands, is one of the smallest primates and has enormous eyes.
Mount Pinatubo's massive 1991 eruption was the second-largest volcanic event of the twentieth century and significantly cooled global temperatures by injecting ash into the stratosphere.
